thread:
incident-bot: [ALERT] grafana: paged-block-manager-prod KV cache bytes jumped 12x in 8m, tail latency for model-worker-prod >5s, error rate up x10. auto-opened incident. dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/kv/kv-cache
maria: oncall here, looking. seeing a deploy of continuous-batching v2 at ~T-10m. rolling windows align with spike.
samir: tail logs from blockmgr: 
```
ERROR block_manager.go:423 metadata leak: block_ref_count 8192 > expected 1024
WARN kv_prefetcher.go:210 prefetch queue grew >1m entries
```
jing: support: we have 1 customer (Acme) with 502s; ticket #12345. trace link in ticket. they report generation timeouts on long contexts.
kairi: initial hypothesis: a batching config change increased in-flight KV requests and prevented normal eviction; paged blocks retained refs -> metadata counters leak -> mem growth -> perf cliff.
maria: agreed. immediate mitigations I propose:
- turn off continuous-batching hot path (set `batching.enabled=false`)
- lower `batch_max_tokens` to 64 for canary pool
- make blockmgr eviction aggressive: `eviction.soft_limit=0.6`
- coordinated rolling restart of affected workers (one AZ at a time)
are we ok to push these as a hotfix? :warning:
samir: +1. logs show `block_alloc` rose steadily after batch change. eviction not keeping up.
kairi: note: prefetched KV entries have strong refs from prefetcher; we should throttle prefetcher immediately. `prefetch.limit=1000`
maria: applying canary config now. patch: 
```
curl -X PATCH https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/runtime/configs/paged-block-manager \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"batching.enabled": false, "batch_max_tokens": 64, "eviction.soft_limit": 0.6, "prefetch.limit": 1000}'
```
(deploy-bot will post status)
deploy-bot: config patch started for cluster paged-block-manager-prod (canary) :gear:
samir: watching metrics. KV cache growth rate flattened within 90s of canary patch. error rate down ~60% on canary nodes.
luca: good catch. We should also disable the new prefetch heuristic that tries to pin long-context KV slices; that's probably the metadata leak vector. Will open PR for revert.
maria: initiating rolling restart for the remaining workers in pool B. doing one node at a time to avoid capacity loss.
samir: after first restart, tail latency dropped from 5.3s -> 0.8s on that node. error rate trending down cluster-wide.
jing: support updated Acme with interim mitigation and ETA for full resolution. ticket updated with stack traces and mitigation steps.
kairi: next steps:
- short postmortem draft (owner: luca)
- patch prefetch heuristic + unit tests (owner: luca)
- revisit batching default with perf benchmarks (owner: samir)
- add metric alert for metadata-ref-count > 2048 (owner: maria)
maria: i'm handing off active incident to @luca for overnight continuity. please use this thread for async updates.
luca: taking over. I will coordinate postmortem and backport fix to stable. added as incident-owner in ops. :white_check_mark:
maria: thanks team. leaving notes in runbook and alert playbook. triage: customer impact limited to some long-context requests and 1 escalated ticket, no data loss.
incident-bot: incident marked as mitigated by manual hotfix at 1987654375. follow-ups tracked in #postmortems and jira: RW-INC-8471
